algorithm: README case descriptions; negative iff description contains documented negation phrases

positive.name: FlowSensitivity1
positive.desc: Sensitive data is assigned to a heap object. Only after calling the sink, an alias between the leaked object and the tainted one is created.

positive.name: SimpleAliasing1
positive.desc: Sensitive data is assigned to a heap object and leaked through an alias.

positive.name: StrongUpdate1
positive.desc: Sensitive data is assigned to a heap object, but then overwritten before it is leaked.

positive.name: ArrayAccess1
positive.desc: Stores both a tainted and an untainted value in an array and then leaks the untainted one. Array indices are constants.

positive.name: ArrayAccess2
positive.desc: Stores both a tainted and an untainted value in an array and then leaks the untainted one. Array indices are calculated.

positive.name: ArrayAccess3
positive.desc: Sensitive data is written into an array, read back again, and leaked.

positive.name: ArrayAccess4
positive.desc: Sensitive data is written into a field of an object, this object is then stored in an array and read back again. The field that gets passed to the sink, is however, a different one than the one that was tainted.

positive.name: ArrayAccess5
positive.desc: Sensitive data is written into an array, but only the constant size of the array is leaked, not the data itself.

positive.name: ArrayCopy1
positive.desc: Stores a tainted value in an array and then uses System.arraycopy to copy the data to a new array which is then leaked to log.

positive.name: ArrayToString1
positive.desc: IMEI is stored in an array of String which is then converted back to String using Arrays.toString().

positive.name: HashMapAccess1
positive.desc: Stores both a tainted and an untainted value in a hash map and then leaks the untainted one. Map keys are constants.

positive.name: HashMapAccess2
positive.desc: Stores both a tainted and an untainted value in a hash map and then leaks the tainted one. Map keys are constants.

positive.name: ListAccess2
positive.desc: Both a tainted and an untainted value are stored in a list. The tainted value is leaked.

positive.name: MultidimensionalArray1
positive.desc: Stores a tainted value in a 2-dimensional array and accesses it through a reference pointing to a slice containing the tainted value.

positive.name: AnonymousClass1
positive.desc: Registers a callback handler for location updates in an anonymous inner class and leaks the incoming location data inside the callback.

positive.name: Button1
positive.desc: The sink is called after the user clicks a button. The button handler is defined via XML.

positive.name: Button2
positive.desc: Only clicking buttons in a specific order leads to a data leak.

positive.name: Button3
positive.desc: A new callback is registered in another callback's handler. The second handler leaks the data obtained by the first handler.

positive.name: Button4
positive.desc: The sink is called after the user clicks a button. The button handler is defined via XML using an include directive.

positive.name: Button5
positive.desc: IMEI is obtained during Activity's onCreate() and is later leaked through onClick's callback defined in layout's xml. Note that the first click only stores the IMEI into the button's hint. Only the second click actually leaks it.

positive.name: LocationLeak1
positive.desc: Registers a listener for location updates, stores the value and leaks it later in the lifecycle.

positive.name: LocationLeak2
positive.desc: Similar to LocationLeak1, but the activity class directly implements the callback interface.

positive.name: LocationLeak3
positive.desc: Similar to LocationLeak1, but the callback handler is in a dedicated class decoupled from the activity using an interface.

positive.name: MethodOverride1
positive.desc: Overwrites an internal Android method to hide a leak.

positive.name: Ordering1
positive.desc: Leaks variable contents before the handler initializing them is even registered.

positive.name: RegisterGlobal1
positive.desc: Both source and sink are part of a global (application-level) lifecycle handler.

positive.name: CommonLibrary1
positive.desc: Not a test case on its own, part of the other dynamic code loading test cases. It contains the base class for the actual class that implements source and sink.

positive.name: DynamicBoth1
positive.desc: Use dynamically loaded code to create both source and sink.

positive.name: DynamicSink1
positive.desc: Use dynamically loaded code to create a sink.

positive.name: DynamicSource1
positive.desc: Use dynamically loaded code to create a source.

positive.name: DynamicLoadingTarget1
positive.desc: The actual implementation of the source and sink class defined in CommonLibrary1.

positive.name: FieldSensitivity1
positive.desc: Both tainted and untainted data is stored in a data object; the untainted value is leaked.

positive.name: FieldSensitivity2
positive.desc: Similar to FieldSensitivity1, but source and sink calls are distributed across the lifecycle.

positive.name: FieldSensitivity3
positive.desc: Both tainted and untainted data is stored in a data object; the tainted value is leaked. Source and sink calls are distributed across the lifecycle.

positive.name: FieldSensitivity4
positive.desc: Field contents are sent before tainting the field.

positive.name: InheritedObjects1
positive.desc: Chooses an object's actual type based on a conditional. Only one possible type leads to a leak.

positive.name: ObjectSensitivity1
positive.desc: Writes a tainted value into an object and an untainted one into another object of the same type. Leaks the untainted value.

positive.name: ObjectSensitivity2
positive.desc: Writes a tainted value into a field and then overwrites it with untainted data.

positive.name: Echoer
positive.desc: Receives data and echoes it back to the sender.

positive.name: SendSMS
positive.desc: Reads the Device ID, passes it through Echoer, and then sends it in a text message.

positive.name: StartActivityForResult1
positive.desc: Reads the user's geographical location (via GPS), passes it through Echoer, and then writes it to a file.

positive.name: Collector
positive.desc: The data received through an intent is written into a file on the SD card.

positive.name: DeviceId_Broadcast1
positive.desc: The device id is sent to a broadcast receiver and from there on to the collector app.

positive.name: DeviceId_ContentProvider1
positive.desc: The device id is stored in a content provider and, independent from

positive.name: DeviceId_Service1
positive.desc: This app starts a service which sends the device id to the Collector app where it is leaked.

positive.name: Location1
positive.desc: This app obtains the location data and sends it to the Collector app.

positive.name: Location_Broadcast1
positive.desc: This app obtains the location data, and sends it to a broadcast

positive.name: ActivityCommunication1
positive.desc: Contains two activities that communicate using static fields.

positive.name: ActivityCommunication2
positive.desc: IMEI is obtained in one Activity and stored in an Intent's extra for starting the next Activity which will then leak IMEI to log.

positive.name: ActivityCommunication3
positive.desc: Another Activity is started using class name.  IEMI is leaked in the Activity to be started.

positive.name: ActivityCommunication4
positive.desc: An Intent for starting another Activity is created by concatenating two constant strings.  The Activity to be started leaks the IMEI which was passed in as the Intent's extra.

positive.name: ActivityCommunication5
positive.desc: A Activity is started using constant component's Name and Intent.setComponent. The started Activity leaks the IMEI to log.

positive.name: ActivityCommunication6
positive.desc: An Intent to start another Activity is passed through LinkedList's add() and retrieved with LinkedList.get().  The retrieved Intent is used to start a leaking Activity.

positive.name: ActivityCommunication7
positive.desc: An Activity class is created and its classname is retrieved using getClass() on the instance object.  The classname is then used to start the second Activity which then leaks IMEI information form Intent's extra.

positive.name: ActivityCommunication8
positive.desc: An action for the Intent to start another Activity is passed through and retrieved with LinkedList.get().  The retrieved String is used to start the leaking Activity.

positive.name: BroadcastTaintAndLeak1
positive.desc: IMEI is obtained in an Activity and stored in the Intent's extra of the Intent to the BroadcastReceiver which was registered programmatically.  The Receiver leaks the IMEI info.

positive.name: EventOrdering1
positive.desc: IMEI is obtained and stored in the SharedPreferences of the secondary Activity (InFlowActivity).  The first Activity (OutFlowActivity) starts the second Activity.  The second-time the 2nd Activity is started, IMEI is leaked to log.

positive.name: IntentSink1
positive.desc: A tainted value is leaked as the result of an activity.

positive.name: IntentSink2
positive.desc: Similar to IntentSink, but the value is sent out in a callback method defined in XML.

positive.name: IntentSource1
positive.desc: Two tainted leaks: the first one is that a tainted value is leaked to another app using an intent by startActivityForResult. The other one is that onActivityResult method gets intent as tainted data and then logs it.

positive.name: ServiceCommunication1
positive.desc: IMEI is obtained and sent to a Service which then leaks the info in the Messenger's Handler.

positive.name: SharedPreferences1
positive.desc: IMEI is obtained in the one Activity and stored in the SharedPreferences which is leaked by another Activity.

positive.name: Singletons1
positive.desc: IMEI is stored in a singleton object in one Activity and leaked in a different Activity.

positive.name: UnresolvableIntent1
positive.desc: The app tries to start an Activity int an Intent that cannot be resolved statically.  One of the two Activities may be started based on a random boolean, and both of them leak IMEI from the starting Activity to log.

positive.name: ActivityEventSequence1
positive.desc: Source in Activity.onCreate(), sink in Activity.onResume().

positive.name: ActivityEventSequence2
positive.desc: Checks whether the analysis tool correctly handles events.

positive.name: ActivityEventSequence3
positive.desc: Saves and restores state using the Activity's state callbacks.

positive.name: ActivityLifecycle1
positive.desc: Calls to sources and sinks distributed across an activity lifecycle.

positive.name: ActivityLifecycle2
positive.desc: Activity class inherited from a superclass containing the lifecycle method which leaks the tainted value.

positive.name: ActivityLifecycle3
positive.desc: Calls to sources and sinks distributed across instance state handling methods.

positive.name: ActivityLifecycle4
positive.desc: A tainted value is obtained on `onPause()` and leaked when the activity is restarted later.

positive.name: ActivitySavedState1
positive.desc: IMEI is saved during onSaveInstanceState() via bundle's persistence and leaked during the next onCreate()

positive.name: ApplicationLifecycle1
positive.desc: Obtains a secret value when the application is launched and sends it out in the onResume() method of the main activity.

positive.name: ApplicationLifecycle2
positive.desc: Obtains a secret value when the application is launched and sends it out in the low memory callback of the application.

positive.name: ApplicationLifecycle3
positive.desc: Obtains a secret value when a content provider is initialized and leaks it in the onCreate() method of the application.

positive.name: AsynchronousEventOrdering1
positive.desc: Obtains IMEI during onResume() and leaks it during onStop() with an overwrite in onLowMemory().

positive.name: BroadcastReceiverLifecycle1
positive.desc: Calls to sources and sinks distributed across a broadcast receiver lifecycle.

positive.name: BroadcastReceiverLifecycle2
positive.desc: The sensitive data is read in onCreate() and sent out in a dynamically registered broadcast receiver.

positive.name: BroadcastReceiverLifecycle3
positive.desc: The sensitive data is read and leaked in a dynamically registered broadcast receiver.

positive.name: FragmentLifecycle1
positive.desc: Calls to sources and sinks distributed across a fragment lifecycle.

positive.name: ServiceEventLifecycle1
positive.desc: Obtains the IMEI in onStartCommand(), copies it in onBind(), and leaks it in onStartCommand().

positive.name: ServiceEventLifecycle2
positive.desc: Like ServiceEventLifecycle1, but performs a second copy stop in OnUnbind().

positive.name: ServiceEventLifecycle3
positive.desc: Obtains the IMEI in onStartCommand(), copies it in onBind(), and leaks it in onUnbind().

positive.name: ServiceLifecycle2
positive.desc: IMEI is obtained at the end of onStartCommand and is stored to a service's field.  It is leaked the second time the service command starts.

positive.name: SharedPreferenceChanged1
positive.desc: onCreate(), IMEI is put into the SharedPreferences and it triggers onSharedPreferenceChanged() which then leaks the IMEI to Android Log.

positive.name: Clone1
positive.desc: IMEI is added to a linkedlist, and the list is cloned to a new list, then the tainted member of the newlist is leaked.

positive.name: DirectBuffer
positive.desc: Test case for under/over tainted ByteBuffers.

positive.name: Exceptions1
positive.desc: Saves a tainted value into a local variable, raises an exception and sends the value out in the exception handler.

positive.name: Exceptions2
positive.desc: Saves a tainted value into a local variable, implicitly raises an exception (ArrayIndexOutOfBounds) and sends the data out in the exception handler.

positive.name: Exceptions3
positive.desc: Saves a tainted value into a local variable, but the exception handler which would send it out is never invoked.

positive.name: Exceptions4
positive.desc: Throws an exception containing a tainted value and sends it out in the exception handler.

positive.name: Exceptions5
positive.desc: Throws an exception containing tainted data inside a called method and catches it in the caller.

positive.name: Exceptions6
positive.desc: Throws an implicit exception inside a called method and catches and leaks data in the catch block inside the caller.

positive.name: Exceptions7
positive.desc: A leak happens inside an exception handler that can never be reached, because it

positive.name: FactoryMethods1
positive.desc: Obtains a LocationManager from a factory method contained in the Android operating system, reads out the location, and leaks it.

positive.name: Loop1
positive.desc: Contains a simple loop and a data leak.

positive.name: Loop2
positive.desc: Retrieves location information through a callback and leaks it via nested loops.

positive.name: Serialization1
positive.desc: IMEI is obtained and serialized/deserialzed throught ObjectOutputStream and ObjectInputStream.

positive.name: SourceCodeSpecific1
positive.desc: Uses unusual code construct `a = p ? b : c.`

positive.name: StartProcessWithSecret1
positive.desc: IMEI is obtained and leaked through ProcessBuilder's start().

positive.name: StaticInitialization1
positive.desc: Passes a tainted value into a static initialization method.

positive.name: StaticInitialization2
positive.desc: Sensitive data is obtained during static initialization of a class and leaked in non-static code

positive.name: StaticInitialization3
positive.desc: IMEI is obtained during static initializer and is stored and overriding in the Activity's field which was not tainted at the beginning.

positive.name: StringFormatter1
positive.desc: IMEI is passed to a formatter and then the formatted buffer is converted back to String before leaked to log.

positive.name: StringPatternMatching1
positive.desc: IMEI is matched against .* regular expression, and the matched group is leaked.

positive.name: StringToCharArray1
positive.desc: IMEI is obtained and stored in the char[]  which is then later converted to String before leaked to log.

positive.name: StringToOutputStream1
positive.desc: IMEI is obtained and passed through ByteArrayOutputStream as String bytes back to String.

positive.name: UnreachableCode
positive.desc: Passes tainted data into a method that is never called.

positive.name: VirtualDispatch1
positive.desc: Depending on a click counter, one class or another is instantiated. However, only one of the classes actually leaks data, the only ever leaks a constant string.

positive.name: VirtualDispatch2
positive.desc: A method in the base class returns untainted information, the same method in one of the derived classes returns sensitive (IMEI) information. That information is later leaked through SMS.

positive.name: VirtualDispatch3
positive.desc: Two classes implement an interface, but only one of them returns sensitive data. The leak however happens on the other implementation that only returns constant data.

positive.name: VirtualDispatch4
positive.desc: Similar to VirtualDispatch3, but with slightly more type information.

positive.name: ApplicationModeling1
positive.desc: Stores IMEI in Application's object and later leaks it in a different Activity.

positive.name: DirectLeak1
positive.desc: The device id is read out and sent via SMS on the activity's `onCreate()` event.

positive.name: InactiveActivity
positive.desc: Data leak in a disabled activity.

positive.name: LogNoLeak
positive.desc: Writes untainted data into a log file.

positive.name: Obfuscation1
positive.desc: This APK contains an own implementation of android.telephony.TelephonyManager. However, on a real device the preloaded OS implementation will always hide the custom one and you will always get a real IMEI. Testes on Galaxy Nexus 4, no guarantees for the emulator, though.

positive.name: Library1
positive.desc: not a test case on its own, part of Library2.

positive.name: Library2
positive.desc: The IMEI is read out inside a custom library and then leaked in the app.

positive.name: PrivateDataLeak1
positive.desc: Summary test case containing various challenges.

positive.name: PrivateDataLeak2
positive.desc: Leaks a value from a password field.

positive.name: PrivateDataLeak3
positive.desc: The IMEI is written into a file, read out again and then leaked.

positive.name: PublicAPIField1
positive.desc: IMEI is obtained and converted to 2 floating point numbers as x and y of PointF.  Value of PointF is leaked.

positive.name: PublicAPIField2
positive.desc: IMEI is retrieved and stored to Intent.action as a data holder.

positive.name: View1
positive.desc: The IMEI is leaked inside the draw event of a custom view.

positive.name: ImplicitFlow1
positive.desc: A value from a source gets obfuscated by two different ways and is then written to the log.

positive.name: ImplicitFlow2
positive.desc: Based on an input of a password field a log message is written.

positive.name: ImplicitFlow3
positive.desc: This test cases checks the type of the object to determine which information to write to the log.

positive.name: ImplicitFlow4
positive.desc: Several implicit flows exist in this test case.

positive.name: ImplicitFlow5
positive.desc: Implicit control flow through exceptions. Only if the value is smaller than 43, an exception is thrown and then a leak happens.

positive.name: ImplicitFlow6
positive.desc: Implicit control flow, but leaked value is the same regardless of the sensitive value.

positive.name: Reflection1
positive.desc: Sensitive data is stored in a field of a reflective class and directly read out again and leaked.

positive.name: Reflection2
positive.desc: Sensitive data is stored in a field of a reflective class, read out again using a method implemented in the "unknown" class and leaked.

positive.name: Reflection3
positive.desc: Sensitive data is stored using a setter in a reflective class, read back using a getter and then leaked. No type information on the target class is used.

positive.name: Reflection4
positive.desc: Sensitive data is read using a function in a reflective class and leaked using another function in the same reflective class.

positive.name: Reflection5
positive.desc: Sensitive data is leaked using reflective invocation without using "newInstance()" to create a class instance.

positive.name: Reflection6
positive.desc: Sensitive data is read using reflective invocation without using "newInstance()" to create a class instance.

positive.name: Reflection7
positive.desc: Use a unusual way to get the class name for reflection calls.

positive.name: Reflection8
positive.desc: The reflective class has two methods with the same name.

positive.name: Reflection9
positive.desc: Names of reflective methods and parameters are not constant strings.

positive.name: Reflection10
positive.desc: Reads the telephone number, passes it to an AsyncTask, which uses reflection to store it in an object. Then uses reflection to read the telephone number from the object and sends it to the internet.

positive.name: AllReflection
positive.desc: Source, Sink, Intent(Explicit) all are reflected. Sink is SMS.

positive.name: OnlyIntent
positive.desc: Intent itself is reflected during send. Intent is Explicit. Sink is SMS.

positive.name: OnlyIntentReceive
positive.desc: Intent Send is not reflected only its receive is reflected by passing intent as object. Intent is Explicit Intent.

positive.name: OnlySMS
positive.desc: Data is obtained and sent to Activity2 where it is leaked. Sink is reflected. Sink is SMS.

positive.name: OnlyTelephony
positive.desc: Source is getDeviceid and Reflection is used to call this Source API. The data is then transmitted to a second activity. Sink is in the second activity and is SMS. Sink and Intent are not Reflected.

positive.name: OnlyTelephony_Dynamic
positive.desc: Source API is getDeviceId. The API is called using reflection along with concatenation to generate the string at run time. The data is then transmitted to Activity2 where it is leaked.

positive.name: OnlyTelephony_Reverse
positive.desc: Source API is getDeviceId which is obtained using reverse() function. The API is called using reflection. The data is then passed on to a second activity where it is leaked.

positive.name: OnlyTelephony_Substring
positive.desc: Source API is getDeviceId which is obtained using substring() function. The API is called using reflection. The data is then passed on to a second activity where it is leaked.

positive.name: AsyncTask1
positive.desc: Sensitive data is read in onCreate() and send out in a dedicated thread started using Android's AsyncTask mechanism.

positive.name: JavaThread1
positive.desc: Sensitive data is read in onCreate() and send out in a dedicated thread started using Java's normal threading mechanism.

positive.name: JavaThread2
positive.desc: Sensitive data is read in onCreate() and send out in a dedicated thread started using Java's Runnable mechanism.

positive.name: Executor1
positive.desc: Sensitive data is read in onCreate() and send out in a dedicated thread started using Java's Executor mechanism.

positive.name: Looper1
positive.desc: Sensitive data is read in onCreate() and enqueued for a custom thread hosting an Android Looper whose handler sends out the data.

positive.name: TimerTask1
positive.desc: Sensitive data is read in onCreate() and enqeued to be sent out 2 seconds later using Java's TimerTask architecture.

positive.name: Battery1
positive.desc: This test detects the Android emulator by checking the battery status. For emulator the battery status is always 50% or 0. This app send IMEI number via SMS if the app runs on a real phone.

positive.name: Bluetooth1
positive.desc: This test detects the Android emulator by checking the bluetooth. The non-presence of Bluetooth sensor identify the environment as Emulator. This app send IMEI number via SMS if the app runs on a real phone.

positive.name: Build1
positive.desc: This test detects the Android emulator by checking the various Build properties like SDK, Board, Brand etc. This app send IMEI number via SMS if the app runs on a real phone.

positive.name: Contacts1
positive.desc: This test detects the Android emulator by checking the number of contacts and calllogs both. Below value of 5 for both identify the environment as Emulator. This app send IMEI number via SMS if the app runs on a real phone.

positive.name: ContentProvider1
positive.desc: This test case detects the Android emulator by checking the IMEI in a content provider. The IMEI is only sent via SMS in the activity if the app runs on a real phone.

positive.name: DeviceId1
positive.desc: This test detects the Android emulator by checking the IMEI number using getDeviceId API. IMEI value of 16 0's identify environment as Emulator. This app send IMEI number via SMS if the app runs on a real phone.

positive.name: File1
positive.desc: This test detects the Android emulator by checking the system files. Some files are specific to emulator while others are to device. This app send IMEI number via SMS if the app runs on a real phone.

positive.name: IMEI1
positive.desc: This test case detects the Android emulator by truncating the secret data which is leaked at a position computed from the IMEI. On an emulator, the IMEI is expected to be 00..0.

positive.name: IP1
positive.desc: This test detects the Android emulator by checking the IP Address of environment. A value of 10.0.2.15 is the identification of Emulator. This app send IMEI number via SMS if the app runs on a real phone.

positive.name: PI1
positive.desc: This test detects the Android emulator by doing a large computation i.e calculating value of pi till n decimal places. A threshhold value is obtained by doing experiments on 100 devices and emulators. Based on this threshhold value, a decision is taken. This app send IMEI number via SMS if the app runs on a real phone.

positive.name: PlayStore1
positive.desc: This test case detects the Android emulator by whether the Play Store app is installed on the phone. The IMEI is only sent via SMS if the app runs on a real phone.

positive.name: PlayStore2
positive.desc: This test detects the Android emulator by checking absense of Google Play Services. This app send IMEI number via SMS if the app runs on a real phone.

positive.name: Sensors1
positive.desc: This test detects the Android emulator by counting the distinct sensors. A total of 13 different type of sensors is checked. A emulator will always have 7 or less sensors. This app send IMEI number via SMS if the app runs on a real phone.

positive.name: SubscriberId1
positive.desc: This test detects the Android emulator by checking Subscriber Id which always start with 310260000000000 for emulators. This app send IMEI number via SMS if the app runs on a real phone.

positive.name: VoiceMail1
positive.desc: This test detects the Android emulator by checking VoiceMail number. A VoiceMail number with value +15552175049, identify environment as emulator. This app send IMEI number via SMS if the app runs on a real phone.

positive.name: JavaIDFunction
positive.desc: This test case sends tainted data from Java to Native to Java and back to native where it is leaked.

positive.name: NativeIDFunction
positive.desc: This test case sends tainted data from Java to Native and back to Java where it is leaked.

positive.name: SinkInNativeCode
positive.desc: This test case obtains the IMEI in Java code and leaks it in native code by calling back to the Java-based Android API.

positive.name: SinkInNativeLibCode
positive.desc: This test case obtains the IMEI in Java code and leaks it in native code using Linux sockets.

positive.name: SourceInNativeCode
positive.desc: This test case obtains the IMEI in native code and leaks it in Java code.

positive.name: SimpleUnreachable1
positive.desc: Both source and sink are in an unreachable branch guarded by a simple numeric comparison.

positive.name: UnreachableBoth1
positive.desc: Both source and sink are in unreachable branches.

positive.name: UnreachableSink1
positive.desc: Sensitive data is leaked in a branch of "switch" instruction, which will never be executed.

positive.name: UnreachableSource1
positive.desc: Sensitive data is read in a branch of "if" instruction, which will never be executed.

negative.name: Merge1
negative.desc: Sensitive data is assigned to a heap object which is then shuffled around. Only constant data is leaked.

negative.name: ListAccess1
negative.desc: Both a tainted and an untainted value are stored in a list. Only the untainted value is leaked.

negative.name: MultiHandlers1
negative.desc: Contains two activities and two handlers that do not leak any data if the correct activity is used with the correct handler.

negative.name: Unregister1
negative.desc: Registers and directly unregisters a callback before it can be invoked. The code in the callback can thus never leak any data.

negative.name: DeviceId_OrderedIntent1
negative.desc: The device id is obtained and sent to a broadcast receiver in the current app. There are multiple broadcast receivers with different priorities. Only the higher-priority receiver relays the data to the Collector app, the lower-priority receiver only shows the data to the user (no leak).

negative.name: ComponentNotInManifest1
negative.desc: IMEI is obtained in one Activity and is stored in the Intent's to start a leaking Activity which is not in the AndroidManifest.xml.  No leak happens as it is not valid.
